papers.title: Integrated biosensors for monitoring microphysiological systems.
papers.abstract: Microphysiological systems (MPSs), also known as organ-on-a-chip models, aim to recapitulate the functional components of human tissues or organs in vitro. Over the last decade, with the advances in biomaterials, 3D bioprinting, and microfluidics, numerous MPSs have emerged with applications to study diseased and healthy tissue models. Various organs have been modeled using MPS technology, such as the heart, liver, lung, and blood-brain barrier. An important aspect of in vitro modeling is the accurate phenotypical and functional characterization of the modeled organ. However, most conventional characterization methods are invasive and destructive and do not allow continuous monitoring of the cells in culture. On the other hand, microfluidic biosensors enable in-line, real-time sensing of target molecules with an excellent limit of detection and in a non-invasive manner, thereby effectively overcoming the limitation of the traditional techniques. Consequently, microfluidic biosensors have been increasingly integrated into MPSs and used for in-line target detection. This review discusses the state-of-the-art microfluidic biosensors by providing specific examples, detailing their main advantages in monitoring MPSs, and highlighting current developments in this field. Finally, we describe the remaining challenges and potential future developments to advance the current state-of-the-art in integrated microfluidic biosensors.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文综述了微生理系统中的集成生物传感器，但未涉及AI与生物打印的结合。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is a review on biosensors for organ-on-chip, with no AI integration into bioprinting workflow, experimental validation, or autonomous decision-making.

summary_en.motivation: This review summarizes the current state of integrated biosensors for monitoring microphysiological systems.
summary_en.method: The paper discusses specific examples of microfluidic biosensors integrated into MPSs and their advantages.
summary_en.result: It highlights that microfluidic biosensors enable non-invasive, real-time monitoring, but challenges remain.
summary_en.validation: The paper is a review without original experimental validation.

papers.title: Influence of Heat Treatment on Microstructure and Mechanical Properties of AZ61 Magnesium Alloy Prepared by Selective Laser Melting (SLM)
papers.abstract: From previous studies, it is known that the dissolution of β-Mg17Al12 at high temperature and the increase of densities at high pressure after hot isostatic pressing (HIP) are the two main reasons for significant improvement in the ductility of AZ61 magnesium alloy prepared by SLM. However, the mechanism of dissolution of β-Mg17Al12 in SLMed AZ61 magnesium alloy at high temperature is not clear. To illustrate the mechanism of the effect of β-Mg17Al12 dissolution on the ductility of SLMed AZ61 Mg alloy, the effect of solid solution heat treatment (T4) on the microstructure and mechanical properties of SLMed AZ61 was investigated and the kinetic model of β-Mg17Al12 dissolution of SLMed AZ61 magnesium alloy was established. According to the results, there is no significant change in the dissolution of the β-Mg17Al12 with an increase of temperature and time when the T4 temperature is lower than 410 °C. At the optimum solution heat treatment temperature of 410 °C, the dissolution rate is accelerated and the β-Mg17Al12 is completely dissolved after 2 h. In addition, the dissolution rate of β-Mg17Al12 decreases with the increase of dissolution time. The strength of SLMed AZ61 magnesium alloy decreases and the ductility increases as the T4 temperature increases. The strength of the specimens is reduced by grain coarsening (29.2 ± 3.7 μm), but the elongation is increased by 90% compared to SLMed AZ61, due to the effect of β-Mg17Al12 dissolution.

summary_zh.motivation: 揭示β-Mg17Al12溶解对SLM成形AZ61镁合金塑性的影响机制
summary_zh.method: 通过固溶热处理实验并建立β相溶解动力学模型
summary_zh.result: 410°C下β相完全溶解，延伸率提高90%但强度下降
summary_zh.validation: 力学拉伸测试与显微组织表征

summary_en.motivation: To understand the mechanism by which β-Mg17Al12 dissolution affects the ductility of SLM-fabricated AZ61 magnesium alloy.
summary_en.method: Solid solution heat treatment (T4) experiments and kinetic modeling of β-Mg17Al12 dissolution were conducted.
summary_en.result: At the optimal temperature of 410°C, β-Mg17Al12 completely dissolved after 2 hours, increasing elongation by 90% while reducing strength due to grain coarsening.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical testing (tensile) and microstructural analysis via SEM and XRD.
